description: CBCT dental findings schema - single source of truth for QA and extraction.
_visual_evidence_rule: Every object_fields block leads with a 'visual_evidence' string. Every other field in that block must be consistent with what visual_evidence describes -- this applies globally, not per-field, so individual field descriptions below do not repeat it.

_definitions.normal_tooth: The DEFAULT reading for a present tooth, arrived at positively -- not what is left when nothing else matched. A normal tooth shows: a continuous, unbroken enamel outline around the whole crown, with no dark notch eating inward at the occlusal surface, at a proximal contact point, or at the cervical margin; brightness no greater than the enamel of the neighbouring teeth in the same image (enamel is ALREADY very bright, so brightness on its own is never evidence of material -- see _definitions.restoration_types); a continuous root outline with no line crossing it; and a crown clear of bone, upright and in line with its neighbours. TWO DARK FEATURES ARE NORMAL ANATOMY and must never be read as findings: the thin dark line running down the CENTRE of the tooth is the pulp chamber and root canal space, and the thin dark line following the OUTSIDE of the root outline is the periodontal ligament. Normal does not mean perfect -- physiological wear/attrition, mild rotation or crowding, and unremarkable variation in root shape or number all still read normal. Normal here is a statement about the TOOTH only: bone around it is captured by tooth_{fdi}_bone_quality and periodontal_bone_resorption_{arch}, and this field has no value for either, so a tooth with bone loss but no decay and no restorative material still reads normal.
_definitions.restoration_types: BRIGHTNESS + SHAPE CALIBRATION -- settle this before choosing any value: a NATURAL tooth crown is ALREADY very bright on CBCT, because enamel is the densest tissue in the body. That brightness is normal and is NOT by itself evidence of restorative material. Brightness alone does not settle it in either direction: metal and dense cements read far brighter than enamel and throw streak artifact, but tooth-coloured composite and ceramic are made to sit in enamel's own range. Judge brightness, SHAPE and POSITION together. Restorative material has geometry a tooth does not: a uniform shell or block with a SHARP, straight margin against tooth substance, a flat floor or a prepared-cavity outline, and it hides or replaces the structure beneath it. Natural enamel caps the crown only, follows the cusp shape, thins away smoothly at the neck, and the dark canal still shows through beneath it. Compare against the enamel of the neighbouring teeth in the same image as ONE input, not as the whole test: distinctly brighter than they are = restorative material, and you should say so; the same brightness but with a prosthetic outline = still restorative material; the same brightness AND natural tooth shape = a normal unrestored crown. filling = a well-defined radiopaque area confined within the tooth's own crown outline, sitting inside part of a prepared cavity -- it does not replace the whole crown. crown = the ENTIRE visible crown replaced by prosthetic material, uniform radiodensity, different from natural enamel. post_and_core = a distinct radiopaque post extending DOWN INTO the root canal space (thicker/shorter than an RCT fill line, never reaches the apex), topped by a core buildup, usually under a crown. A tooth with a post belongs under post_and_core even if a crown also sits on top -- never double-count as crown.
_definitions.root_canal_fill: A distinctly uniform, sharply-defined radiopaque line running down the CENTER of the canal space, clearly brighter than the surrounding natural root dentin -- not just normal dense dentin or a hollow pulp chamber, and not a crown/post sitting only in the coronal portion.
_definitions.implant_vs_root: An implant is a uniformly bright, sharply-edged, screw/cylinder-shaped metal post embedded directly in bone with a threaded surface, in direct contact with bone (no periodontal-ligament radiolucent line around it, unlike a natural root). Never count a dense natural root as an implant just because it looks radiopaque.
_definitions.impaction_direction: Which way the crown is tipped or displaced, relative to the arch. Judge it on the 3D render from the geometry of the jaw itself -- soft tissue is not rendered, so never look for a tongue or a cheek. normal = the crown is upright and in line with the neighbouring teeth, tipped no more than they are; this is the ANSWER FOR MOST TEETH. When the tooth is ABSENT the answer is null instead, since there is no crown to be tipped and normal would be a claim about a tooth that is not there. mesial = crown tilted toward the front of the arch, often wedged under the back of the adjacent tooth (e.g. 38 against 37), root tilted posteriorly. distal = mirror of mesial. buccal = crown displaced toward the OUTER surface of the jaw, the side of the bone facing away from the midline of the arch (the cheek side). lingual = crown displaced toward the INNER surface of the jaw, the side of the bone facing the middle of the arch (the tongue side in the mandible, the palate side in the maxilla). ALWAYS ANSWERED, not only for an impacted tooth: a wrong orientation is one of the two things that MAKES a tooth impacted, so it is judged first and independently -- see _definitions.impacted.
_definitions.eruption_state: complete_bony_inclusion = no crown surface above bone; the tooth is fully enclosed in bone. partially_erupted = some but not all of the crown exposed. fully_erupted = entire crown clear of bone. absent = no tooth structure present at this position.
_definitions.impacted: An impacted tooth is one that CANNOT ERUPT NORMALLY, or cannot erupt INTO THE RIGHT POSITION. There are therefore two ways to be impacted and either one on its own is enough: (a) the tooth has not fully erupted -- eruption_state is complete_bony_inclusion or partially_erupted, i.e. bone still covers some or all of the crown; (b) the tooth has come up but out of line -- orientation is anything other than normal, i.e. the crown is tipped or displaced mesially, distally, buccally or lingually. A fully erupted tooth tipped hard against its neighbour is impacted under (b) even though (a) does not apply. Decided FROM those two answers, not judged separately: impacted = true when (eruption_state is complete_bony_inclusion or partially_erupted) OR (orientation is not normal); impacted = false only when the tooth is fully_erupted AND its orientation is normal. absent is the one exception, and it is answered with null rather than false: false is the claim "this tooth is not impacted", which presupposes a tooth. Where nothing is segmented there is no claim to make, so eruption_state absent takes impacted = null and orientation = null. The difference is not cosmetic -- postprocessing reads false as a vote AGAINST an impaction another image reported at that position, and null as no vote at all; absence is settled separately, after the vote. So the judgments to make are eruption_state and orientation (see _definitions.eruption_state and _definitions.impaction_direction); impacted follows from them, and all three answers in the same block must agree by this rule.
_definitions.bone_loss_extent: Judged as bone loss relative to root length, from the CEJ (cemento-enamel junction) down to where the bone crest currently sits. none = crest at/near the CEJ. mild = loss <1/3 of root length. moderate = roughly 1/3-2/3. severe = >2/3, root largely unsupported.

mandible.question_text: First describe what you see at the right condyle, then answer: is it included in the scan volume?
mandible.description: The condyle is the rounded knob at the TOP of the mandibular ramus, posterior, articulating with the skull base -- distinct from the pointed/triangular coronoid process which sits anterior. Morphology classification is out of scope; inclusion only.

object_fields.visual_evidence: string -- describe whether a rounded condylar head is visible and whether it's cut off by the volume boundary

Morphology classification is out of scope; inclusion only. Mirrors mandible_condyle_right on the left side.

object_fields.visual_evidence: string -- describe whether a rounded condylar head is visible and whether it's cut off by the volume boundary

mandible.question_text: First describe the right mandibular canal's course and, root by root, the bone between it and the posterior tooth roots above it. Then answer: does the canal run on the lingual or the buccal side of those roots, and does any root apex actually reach the canal? Answer an empty list when every root still has bone between it and the canal, which is the usual case.
mandible.description: location = which side of the mandible the canal runs along, relative to the roots it passes: lingual = the inner surface of the jaw, the side of the bone facing the middle of the arch (tongue side); buccal = the outer surface, facing away from the midline (cheek side). There is no 'regular' value -- the canal always runs to one side or the other, so answer the side you can actually see rather than looking for an abnormality. adjacent_teeth = BASE RATE, READ THIS FIRST: AN EMPTY LIST IS THE NORMAL ANSWER. This is NOT "which teeth are nearest the canal" -- some tooth is always the nearest one, and naming it because it is nearest is a false finding, not a cautious one. What is asked is WHETHER any root apex actually reaches the canal: touching its upper wall, indenting it, or crossing it, with no clear bone left between the two. If every root ends with a visible band of bone between its apex and the canal roof -- however thin -- the list is empty, and that is the answer for most sides. When it does happen it is nearly always a third or second molar, because that is where the canal runs highest and the roots reach deepest; a premolar or canine almost never qualifies. Judge each posterior root on its own and list only the ones that reach the canal.

object_fields.visual_evidence: string -- trace the canal's course and say which side of the roots it passes on; then take the posterior roots it runs under ONE AT A TIME and say, for each, whether a band of bone still separates its apex from the canal or whether the root actually touches or crosses it
object_fields.adjacent_teeth: list[int] -- FDI numbers; empty if none

mandible.question_text: Long-term tooth loss can lead to alveolar bone resorption, which affects future implant or restorative planning. Look for an edentulous area in the mandible (3 or more missing teeth in a row, or the whole arch if the patient has no teeth at all). If one exists, say whether the remaining bone height there shows resorption.
mandible.description: Edentulous area = 3 or more missing teeth in a row, or the whole mandible if completely edentulous (mark this with fully_edentulous). Use the mandibular canal as your main reference for judging atrophy: if the canal sits close to, or exposed at, the ridge crest, that's resorption. If teeth remain nearby to compare against, a ridge height noticeably lower than the roots of those neighboring teeth is also resorption, even if the canal itself still looks deep. If the canal sits well below the crest and (where a comparison is available) the ridge height looks close to neighboring tooth-bearing areas, there's no resorption.

object_fields.visual_evidence: string -- bone height where teeth are missing, compared to nearby areas that still have teeth (if any), and how close the nerve canal is to the top of the ridge
object_fields.present: bool -- true if there's at least one stretch of 3+ missing teeth in a row (or the whole arch is edentulous)
object_fields.fully_edentulous: bool, only when present == true -- true if there are NO teeth left anywhere in this jaw
object_fields.atrophy: bool, only when present == true -- true if the bone height in that edentulous area is reduced, per the canal-proximity/adjacent-root criteria above

mandible.question_text: First describe any small, bulbous teeth typical of the primary dentition, then list which primary teeth are present.
mandible.description: FDI 71-75 (lower left), 81-85 (lower right). Smaller, more bulbous, thinner enamel, shorter flared roots than permanent teeth; often an unerupted permanent crown visible beneath.

object_fields.visual_evidence: string -- describe any such teeth and their positions

mandible.question_text: Find the lower left wisdom tooth -- the lower left third molar, FDI 38, drawn in slate blue (if no slate blue tooth is there, it is not segmented: answer eruption_state absent). Impaction is not a separate judgment -- it follows from those two: a tooth that has not fully erupted is impacted, and so is one that has erupted out of line (orientation not normal). Either one alone is enough.
mandible.description: Independent 3D-render read of tooth 38, whose eruption_state is cross-checked in postprocessing against tooth_38_eruption. This is the ONLY read of this tooth's impaction -- nothing else corroborates it, so answer it on what you can actually see. See _definitions.impacted, _definitions.impaction_direction and _definitions.eruption_state.

mandible.question_text: First describe any uniformly bright, sharply-edged screw/cylinder shapes embedded directly in the mandible bone, quadrant by quadrant. Then answer: how many implants are in quadrant III (31-38)? Quadrant IV (41-48)? For each, describe position, osseointegration, and crown.
mandible.description: See _definitions.implant_vs_root. Go quadrant by quadrant before counting.

object_fields.visual_evidence: string -- per quadrant (III: 31-38, IV: 41-48), describe/count any implant-like structure and its bone interface
object_fields.implants: list[object] -- length must equal quadrant_3_implant_count + quadrant_4_implant_count; each: {fdi_number: int, location: string e.g. 'position 35', osseointegration_status: enum:well|poor -- poor = radiolucent gap along the threaded surface, with_crown: bool}

mandible.question_text: First describe any series of connected, uniformly-bright crown-shaped structures spanning a gap, then answer presence and describe each bridge.
mandible.description: A bridge = connected crowns spanning missing teeth, anchored on natural teeth or implants at each end.

object_fields.visual_evidence: string -- describe any spanning structure and what anchors each end
object_fields.bridges: list[object] -- each: {span_start: int, span_end: int, abutment_teeth: list[int], implant_supported_teeth: list[int], pontic_teeth: list[int], details: string}

mandible.question_text: First describe the mandible's bone texture and flag the single most notable area distinctly brighter or darker than its surroundings, then answer presence, type, and location.
mandible.description: Compare against surrounding trabecular bone, NOT a tooth's own crown/root density (normal root radiopacity is not a bone finding). radiopaque = brighter than surrounding bone (e.g. retained material, sclerotic patch). radiolucent = darker, usually bordered (e.g. cyst, near a root apex or extraction site). Report only the single most notable finding per arch. Cross-checked in postprocessing against tooth_{fdi}_bone_quality for the teeth this location names: the arch-level lesion is reported only where a tooth's own composite read confirms it, since this panoramic read is otherwise the single unverifiable source for it.

object_fields.visual_evidence: string -- describe general trabecular texture and call out the single most notable area (excluding tooth roots/crowns)
object_fields.location: string, only when present == true -- from which tooth to which tooth, by FDI tags

mandible.question_text: First describe the bone crest position relative to the CEJ across the mandibular teeth, then answer extent and pattern.
mandible.description: Arch-level generalization (about bone loss around teeth still present, not edentulous-ridge atrophy). See _definitions.bone_loss_extent. Distinct from the per-tooth bone_loss value in tooth_{fdi}_periodontal_status -- this fact captures the arch-wide pattern (diffuse vs focal, vertical vs horizontal) needed for narrative synthesis.

object_fields.visual_evidence: string -- bone crest position relative to CEJ, as a fraction of root length, across the arch
object_fields.pattern: list[string] -- one or both of vertical, horizontal; only when extent != none. horizontal = even, roughly parallel recession across adjacent teeth. vertical = angular/uneven, steeper along one tooth than its neighbor

maxilla.question_text: Look at the TAN maxillary bone above the upper teeth. First describe whether any tan bone is drawn at all, and if it is, how far up it extends and whether its top edge is cut flat by the volume boundary. Then answer: is the maxilla included in the scan volume?
maxilla.description: JUDGE THE TAN BONE, NOT THE TEETH. Upper teeth are drawn in their own individual colors and are segmented separately from the maxilla, so a row of upper crowns floating above the mandible with no tan behind them means the maxillary bone was NOT in the volume. TWO ANSWERS ONLY. not_included = no tan maxillary bone drawn at all -- upper teeth alone, or nothing above the mandible. included = tan maxillary bone is present, in any amount, typically a band covering part or most of the upper tooth roots with its upper extent cut flat by the volume boundary. There is deliberately no 'fully included' answer: that would require both blue maxillary sinuses to be closed at their superior borders inside the volume, which a dental CBCT essentially never reaches, so the distinction was dropped rather than left as a value to guess at. Any tan bone at all is 'included'. Remember a structure absent from the segmentation is simply not drawn, so missing tan is real absence, not a rendering artifact.

object_fields.visual_evidence: string -- state first whether ANY tan maxillary bone is drawn; if it is, say how far up it extends and whether its top edge is cut flat by the volume boundary. Do not cite upper teeth as evidence that the maxilla is present.
object_fields.maxilla_included: enum:included|not_included -- not_included: no tan maxillary bone drawn, whatever upper teeth are visible. included: any tan maxillary bone present.

maxilla.question_text: First describe, across the coronal and sagittal views, whether the right maxillary sinus's outer boundary is fully closed or only partially visible, then answer scope, mucosa_state, sinus_content, and intrasinusal_teeth.
maxilla.description: This fact is only asked when the sinus has at least some voxels in the scan, so there is no not_included scope value. fully_included = the boundary (including the upper/superior border) is fully closed across both views. partially_included = only part (typically the inferior border) is visible, upper border cut off by the crop. mucosa_state is normal|thickening only (cyst/polypoid intentionally dropped for this fact). Separately check whether a posterior root visibly touches/crosses the sinus floor AND whether its location matches the SAME location as any thickening -- spatial correspondence required, not mere co-occurrence.

object_fields.visual_evidence: string -- trace the boundary across both views noting which borders are closed vs cut off; describe lining and content density; if thickening is present, note where; separately check root-to-floor contact and whether it spatially matches the thickening
object_fields.intrasinusal_teeth: list[int], only when scope == 'fully_included' and mucosa_state == 'thickening' -- FDI 11-18 whose root tip projects into/through the floor at the SAME location as the thickening; empty if not met

maxilla.question_text: First describe, across the coronal and sagittal views, whether the left maxillary sinus's outer boundary is fully closed or only partially visible, then answer scope, mucosa_state, sinus_content, and intrasinusal_teeth.

object_fields.visual_evidence: string -- trace the boundary across both views noting which borders are closed vs cut off; describe lining and content density; if thickening is present, note where; separately check root-to-floor contact and whether it spatially matches the thickening
object_fields.intrasinusal_teeth: list[int], only when scope == 'fully_included' and mucosa_state == 'thickening' -- FDI 21-28 whose root tip projects into/through the floor at the SAME location as the thickening; empty if not met

maxilla.question_text: Long-term tooth loss can lead to alveolar bone resorption, which affects future implant or restorative planning. Look for an edentulous area in the maxilla (3 or more missing teeth in a row, or the whole arch if the patient has no teeth at all). If one exists, say whether the remaining bone height there shows resorption.
maxilla.description: Edentulous area = 3 or more missing teeth in a row, or the whole maxilla if completely edentulous (mark this with fully_edentulous). In the back of the mouth (premolar/molar region), use the maxillary sinus floor as your main reference for judging atrophy: if only a thin amount of bone separates the ridge crest from the sinus floor, that's resorption. In the front of the mouth there's no sinus to check against -- if teeth remain nearby to compare against, a ridge height noticeably lower than the roots of those neighboring teeth is resorption. If no teeth remain anywhere in the arch, judge the front ridge by its own shape instead: a healthy ridge is wide and rounded, a resorbed one is thin like a knife edge or flattened, level with or below the surrounding bone. If there's ample bone between the crest and the sinus floor posteriorly, and (where a comparison is available) the ridge height anteriorly looks close to neighboring tooth-bearing areas, there's no resorption.

object_fields.visual_evidence: string -- bone height where teeth are missing (compared to a nearby tooth-bearing spot if one exists, or judged on its own shape if the whole jaw has no teeth), and in the back of the mouth, how much bone separates the ridge top from the sinus above it
object_fields.present: bool -- true if there's at least one stretch of 3+ missing teeth in a row (or the whole arch is edentulous)
object_fields.fully_edentulous: bool, only when present == true -- true if there are NO teeth left anywhere in this jaw
object_fields.atrophy: bool, only when present == true -- true if the bone height in that edentulous area is reduced, per the sinus-floor/adjacent-root criteria above

ALWAYS answered otherwise, not only when impacted: a non-normal orientation is one of the two things that MAKE a tooth impacted. See _definitions.impaction_direction.

maxilla.question_text: First describe any uniformly bright, sharply-edged screw/cylinder shapes embedded directly in the maxilla bone, quadrant by quadrant. Then answer: how many implants are in quadrant I (11-18)? Quadrant II (21-28)? For each, describe position, osseointegration, and crown.
maxilla.description: See _definitions.implant_vs_root. Go quadrant by quadrant before counting.

object_fields.visual_evidence: string -- per quadrant (I: 11-18, II: 21-28), describe/count any implant-like structure and its bone interface
object_fields.implants: list[object] -- length must equal quadrant_1_implant_count + quadrant_2_implant_count; each: {fdi_number: int, location: string e.g. 'position 15', osseointegration_status: enum:well|poor, with_crown: bool}

maxilla.question_text: First describe any series of connected, uniformly-bright crown-shaped structures spanning a gap, then answer presence and describe each bridge.
maxilla.description: A bridge = connected crowns spanning missing teeth, anchored on natural teeth or implants at each end.

object_fields.visual_evidence: string -- describe any spanning structure and what anchors each end
object_fields.bridges: list[object] -- each: {span_start: int, span_end: int, abutment_teeth: list[int], implant_supported_teeth: list[int], pontic_teeth: list[int], details: string}

maxilla.question_text: First describe the maxilla's bone texture and flag the single most notable area distinctly brighter or darker than its surroundings, then answer presence, type, and location.
maxilla.description: Compare against surrounding trabecular bone, NOT a tooth's own crown/root density (normal root radiopacity is not a bone finding). radiopaque = brighter than surrounding bone (e.g. retained material, sclerotic patch). radiolucent = darker, usually bordered (e.g. cyst, near a root apex or extraction site). Report only the single most notable finding per arch. Cross-checked in postprocessing against tooth_{fdi}_bone_quality for the teeth this location names: the arch-level lesion is reported only where a tooth's own composite read confirms it, since this panoramic read is otherwise the single unverifiable source for it.

object_fields.visual_evidence: string -- describe general trabecular texture and call out the single most notable area (excluding tooth roots/crowns)
object_fields.location: string, only when present == true -- from which tooth to which tooth, by FDI tags

maxilla.question_text: First describe the bone crest position relative to the CEJ across the maxillary teeth, then answer extent and pattern.
maxilla.description: Arch-level generalization (about bone loss around teeth still present, not edentulous-ridge atrophy). See _definitions.bone_loss_extent. Distinct from the per-tooth bone_loss value in tooth_{fdi}_periodontal_status -- this fact captures the arch-wide pattern (diffuse vs focal, vertical vs horizontal) needed for narrative synthesis.

object_fields.visual_evidence: string -- bone crest position relative to CEJ, as a fraction of root length, across the arch
object_fields.pattern: list[string] -- one or both of vertical, horizontal; only when extent != none

dental_elements.question_text: Judge tooth {fdi}'s state -- only mark a flag true if you're confident, not on a maybe.
dental_elements.description: If no crown remains at all, that's a root remnant (is_remnant = true); with_caries/with_fillings/with_full_crown then don't apply (no crown surface left to judge), but with_root_fracture/with_endo/with_post_and_core still can (e.g. a residual post in a fractured root). caries = an irregular dark/radiolucent area in enamel or dentin, starting at the margin and possibly extending toward the pulp. Do not confuse this with (a) the normal, unfilled pulp/root canal space itself -- a small, round, radiolucent (dark) area centered in the root, not itself a finding -- or (b) root canal treatment fill material, which is the OPPOSITE appearance: a radiopaque (bright) line, see _definitions.root_canal_fill. fractured = a line crossing the root's normally continuous structure. fillings = smaller than the crown, usually confined to the margin. full_crown = the whole crown replaced by prosthetic material: uniform density behind a SHARP margin at the neck, hiding the tooth structure under it. Metal reads far brighter than enamel and streaks, but ceramic and composite crowns can read at enamel's own brightness -- so read the outline too: in axial view a crown fills nearly the whole tooth cross-section, while in coronal/sagittal views only the outer shell reads bright, the interior does not. post_and_core = a bright area filling the crown similarly across all three views (axial/coronal/sagittal) PLUS a connected bright post in the root canal that is thick and short (unlike the thin root_canal_fill line) -- both the core and the post must be present to set this true. with_full_crown and with_post_and_core are independent, not mutually exclusive: a post-and-core capped by a full crown should have both set true.

object_fields.visual_evidence: string -- describe the crown surface and root outline for this tooth across the available views, or note if no crown remains at all
object_fields.is_remnant: bool -- true if no crown remains, only root structure
object_fields.with_caries: bool -- true only if a dark/radiolucent area is visible in enamel or dentin per the caries criteria above; false if is_remnant is true
object_fields.with_root_fracture: bool -- true only if a line crosses the root's normally continuous structure
object_fields.with_endo: bool -- true if the canal space or apical area looks distinct enough to warrant a closer look for root canal treatment; gates tooth_{fdi}_endodontic_treatment, which only runs when this is true
object_fields.with_fillings: bool -- true if a smaller, margin-confined radiopaque area is visible per the fillings criteria above; false if is_remnant is true
object_fields.with_full_crown: bool -- true per the full_crown criteria above (axial vs coronal/sagittal appearance); false if is_remnant is true
object_fields.with_post_and_core: bool -- true only if BOTH the core (crown-matching brightness across all views) AND the post (thick, short, connected bright fill in the canal) are present

dental_elements.question_text: First describe how much of the crown sits above versus below the bone line for tooth {fdi}, then answer the eruption state.
dental_elements.description: See _definitions.eruption_state. Use the coronal and sagittal composite panels.

object_fields.visual_evidence: string -- using the coronal and sagittal panels, describe crown exposure above vs below the bone line, or note if absent

dental_elements.question_text: Only answer this fact when tooth_{fdi}_morphology.with_endo == true. First describe exactly what fills the canal space and the area around the root apex for tooth {fdi}, then answer filling quality and whether a periapical lesion is present.
dental_elements.description: Gated by tooth_{fdi}_morphology.with_endo -- presence of root canal treatment is established by that gate, not re-asked here; this fact only characterizes it. See _definitions.root_canal_fill. Separately check the area around the apex for an enlarged dark region beyond the normal thin periodontal ligament line before setting periapical_lesion.

object_fields.visual_evidence: string -- describe the radiopaque fill line in the canal: how far toward the apex it extends and whether it is continuous; separately describe the apical region for any enlarged dark area
object_fields.filling_quality: enum:adequate|inadequate|overfilled|discontinuous -- adequate = full length near the apex, no gaps; inadequate = stops short of the apex; overfilled = extends past the apex; discontinuous = visible gaps/voids
object_fields.periapical_lesion: bool -- true only if an enlarged radiolucent area around the apex, distinctly beyond the normal ligament line, is described

dental_elements.question_text: First locate the CEJ and describe the bone crest position for tooth {fdi}, then answer bone loss extent and furcation involvement.
dental_elements.description: See _definitions.bone_loss_extent, applied to this one tooth. furcation_involvement (multi-rooted teeth only) = bone loss between the roots, visible as a radiolucent notch/triangle where the roots split.

object_fields.visual_evidence: string -- CEJ location and bone crest position as a fraction of root length; for multi-rooted teeth, whether bone fills the furcation notch
object_fields.findings: string -- describe periodontal status, consistent with visual_evidence

dental_elements.question_text: Describe the bone immediately AROUND the root(s) of tooth {fdi} -- not the tooth itself -- then answer whether a distinct radiopaque or radiolucent area is present there.
dental_elements.description: The periapical and peri-radicular bone of this one tooth, at composite resolution. Compare against the trabecular bone elsewhere in the same panel, NOT against the tooth's own crown or root: a normal root is denser than bone and is not a bone finding, and the dark periodontal ligament line following the root outline is normal anatomy, not a lesion. radiopaque = distinctly brighter than surrounding trabecular bone (sclerotic patch, retained material). radiolucent = distinctly darker and usually bordered (cyst, periapical rarefaction, extraction socket). Answer present = false unless the area is unmistakable -- most teeth sit in unremarkable bone. This is the SECOND source for bone_quality_{arch}: postprocessing reports that arch-level lesion only for teeth this per-tooth read confirms, so a false positive here manufactures a lesion in the report and a false negative merely withholds one.

object_fields.visual_evidence: string -- describe the trabecular bone around this tooth's root(s) and apex, and say explicitly whether it matches the bone elsewhere in the panel or differs from it
object_fields.present: bool -- true only if visual_evidence describes a distinct brighter or darker area in the BONE around this tooth

dental_elements.question_text: Read ONLY the coronal row (the middle row) of tooth {fdi}'s composite. First describe, in those panels alone, where the mandibular canal sits between the buccal and the lingual cortical plate, and root by root how much bone lies between tooth {fdi}'s apices and the canal. Then answer which plate the canal runs closer to, and whether a root of THIS tooth actually reaches it.
dental_elements.description: Asked for the lower molars only (36-38, 46-48) -- the canal runs beneath them, and there is nothing to judge at a position it does not pass. ONE ROW ONLY: answer from the coronal panels. A coronal cut is the only one that shows both cortical plates and the canal in the same picture; the axial row is cut at crown/mid/root height and zoomed differently, and the sagittal row cuts ALONG the canal rather than across it, so neither can show a buccal-lingual position at all. In those coronal panels the canal is the structure filled with the translucent YELLOW wash (see the image caption); if no yellow appears anywhere in the row the canal was not segmented for this side, and you are then reading the canal itself -- a round, dark, cortically outlined tube in the bone below the roots. location = which cortical plate the canal lies CLOSER to, compared as the shortest distance from the canal's outer border to the INNER surface of that plate: lingual = the plate facing the middle of the arch (tongue side), buccal = the plate facing away from the midline (cheek side). It is a comparison between the two distances, not a threshold and not an abnormality: the canal is always nearer one plate than the other, so answer the side you can see is closer; there is no 'central' value. adjacent_to_teeth = BASE RATE, READ THIS FIRST: FALSE IS THE NORMAL ANSWER. This is NOT "is tooth {fdi} near the canal" -- under a molar the canal always runs somewhere below the roots, and answering true because it is nearby is a false finding, not a cautious one. True means a root of THIS tooth reaches the canal: touching its wall, indenting it, or crossing it, with no clear bone left between the two. If every root of tooth {fdi} ends with a visible band of bone between its apex and the canal -- however thin -- the answer is false, and that is the answer for most molars. Judge tooth {fdi}'s own roots only: a neighbouring molar's root reaching the canal in the same panel is not this tooth's finding. This is the same judgement mandible_canal_right/mandible_canal_left make for a whole side, asked here one tooth at a time and read off the coronal cut instead of the 3D render.

object_fields.visual_evidence: string -- from the coronal panels only: where the canal sits between the buccal and the lingual plate and which one it is nearer; then, root by root, whether a band of bone still separates tooth {fdi}'s apex from the canal or whether the root touches or crosses it
object_fields.location: enum:lingual|buccal -- the plate whose inner surface is the shorter distance from the canal's outer border
object_fields.adjacent_to_teeth: bool -- true only if a root of tooth {fdi} touches, indents or crosses the canal with no bone left between them

_derived_from.why: uniform-32 asks every fact against the same 32 slices, so the schema's cross-source redundancy buys no extra signal -- only tokens and self-contradiction

removed_facts.dental_arch_findings_mandible: per-tooth findings map covered by tooth_{fdi}_morphology + _endodontic_treatment + _eruption, and its wisdom-only `impacted` value by lower_{left,right}_wisdom_tooth
removed_facts.dental_arch_findings_maxilla: per-tooth findings map covered by tooth_{fdi}_morphology + _endodontic_treatment + _eruption, and its wisdom-only `impacted` value by upper_{left,right}_wisdom_tooth

kept_despite_looking_redundant.lower_left_wisdom_tooth: since v6.3 there is no tooth_{fdi}_impaction, so with dental_arch_findings_{arch} removed these four facts are the ONLY source of impaction; tooth_{fdi}_eruption duplicates their eruption_state but not `orientation` or `impacted`
kept_despite_looking_redundant.periodontal_bone_resorption_mandible: only source of `pattern` (vertical/horizontal), which synthesize_report.py renders
